**Project type:** Local Python research and reproducibility workflow for strong gravitational lens image processing, controlled simulations, classical lens recovery, and early machine-learning regression.

> This is an evidence-based description of the repository and its on-disk artifacts at the snapshot date. Numerical outcomes are taken from existing release records and reports; they were not recomputed for this document. No test suite was run while preparing this summary.

## 1. Executive summary

Lensing builds auditable workflows around strong gravitational lens images. It brings real CASTLES FITS observations and synthetic lens simulations into a shared, versioned CSV manifest contract. Its first supervised target is the angular Einstein radius, theta_E_arcsec, in arcseconds. The repository contains:

- FITS metadata extraction, curated catalogue joins, standardization, masks, background and variance products, release validation, and human review previews for actual observations.
- A simulator ladder from analytic SIS controls through SIE/Sersic scenes, observation effects, noise, and broader stress settings.
- Deterministic product validation, artifact checksums, and splits that keep related ancestry together.
- Bounded classical recovery experiments and an exploratory three-system real-image astrometric comparison.
- A PyTorch image-only CNN baseline, a frozen synthetic test evaluation, a three-seed validation benchmark, two Huber-delta ablations, and paired reports.
- Scientific boundary documentation, schema definitions, versioned configurations, result tables, diagnostic plots, and an ML planning notebook.

The repository demonstrates a reproducible **synthetic in-domain engineering baseline**. It does **not** establish calibrated physical-mass inference, calibrated posterior uncertainty, population performance, or accuracy on real HST/CASTLES images. The documented reasons are substantive: local actual observations lack empirical PSF, ERR and DQ products; their variance fallback is explicitly toy/unprofiled; simulations use analytic source profiles and Gaussian PSFs; priors are hand-set engineering ranges; and the real comparison is small and preselected.

## Reader’s guide: what this project does, from first principles

### The astronomical problem

In a strong gravitational lens, a massive foreground galaxy lies between us and a more distant bright object. The foreground mass bends the background object’s light. Depending on alignment and mass distribution, one background source can appear as two or more separate points, stretched arcs, or a nearly complete ring. These are multiple appearances of the same source, not necessarily separate objects. NASA’s Hubble overview gives an accessible visual introduction, and a technical review explains the image mapping and Einstein-ring geometry: [NASA: Hubble’s Gravitational Lenses](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/science/universe-uncovered/hubbles-gravitational-lenses/) and [Essentials of Strong Gravitational Lensing](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11214-024-01041-w).

A simplified description maps a position in the observed image plane to a position in the background source plane:

    beta = theta - alpha(theta)

Here theta is an observed angular position, beta is the corresponding source position without lensing, and alpha is deflection caused by the foreground mass. For a given beta, there can be multiple valid theta positions. When source, lens and observer are especially well aligned, the images can form a ring; its characteristic angular radius is called the Einstein radius. Real lenses are rarely perfect circles: elliptical mass distributions, source offsets, foreground galaxy light and observing conditions turn the ring into arcs or separate images.

This project first estimates the characteristic **angular scale** theta_E_arcsec from an image. Arcseconds are angles on the sky. An angular Einstein radius is not itself a mass in solar masses: mass inference also requires the lens/source distance geometry (normally redshifts plus a cosmology), a specified mass model and, for enclosed mass, a stated aperture. The schema keeps catalogue estimates, simulated model parameters and physical mass separate so one cannot silently substitute for another.

### What one astronomical image contains

An observed image is not simply a picture of the lens. Its pixel values combine source light after lensing, foreground lens-galaxy light, sky/background, telescope blur and detector noise:

    measured pixels ≈ blurred lensed source + foreground lens light
                      + background + detector/read noise

The blur is described by the point-spread function (PSF), which depends on telescope, instrument, filter and observing conditions. FITS files may contain several image planes and headers with units, exposure and coordinate information. Invalid or uncovered pixels need masks. The project therefore aims to preserve the science image, model-ready image, masks, variance/noise description, PSF and geometry as separate traceable products instead of keeping only an anonymous normalized image.

The actual-data branch starts from CASTLES FITS observations and curated system labels. It standardizes their shape and records what is known or unknown about instrument, units, scale, redshifts and suitability. The real release is useful for preprocessing and quality control, but its missing empirical PSF/error/quality planes and toy variance prevent calibrated pixel-likelihood claims.

### Why simulated images are part of the project

Supervised training needs a target value known for each training image. Real telescope images do not provide exact true Einstein radii for every system. A simulator addresses that engineering problem: choose a lens and source, render lensed light, add observing effects, and save the parameters used to create the image. Because the generator chose theta_E, the simulation manifest can carry an exact label.

The simulator progresses through increasingly complex scenes:

- **SIS (singular isothermal sphere):** a symmetric analytic control for checking geometry and recovery.
- **SIE (singular isothermal ellipsoid):** an elliptical mass model that creates less symmetric image configurations.
- **Sersic source:** a parameterized extended brightness profile for a galaxy source; some scenes also include point-like lensed images.
- **Observation model:** foreground lens light, Gaussian PSF, background, Poisson counting variation and read noise are added to the lensed scene.
- **Stress cases:** wider shape, shear, brightness, PSF and noise ranges probe beyond the main engineering proposal.

The progression is intentional: first check model conventions, then add an extended source, then image formation and noise, then broader settings. The 1,000-parent engineering set uses the validated middle/observation-stage proposal. Its P100 stress examples stay separate so the main training distribution is not quietly changed.

Simulation is a controlled approximation, not a replacement for the telescope. The generated galaxies are analytic, PSFs are Gaussian and detector noise is simplified. A model may learn physical geometric cues, regularities specific to the simulator, or both. Reports therefore call the current score **in-domain synthetic performance** and reserve real-domain claims for future work.

### What question the CNN answers

The CNN is an image-to-number regressor. It receives one 256 × 256 image channel and returns one predicted angular Einstein radius. During training, software compares that prediction with the simulator’s saved theta_E and adjusts network weights. It selects the checkpoint on validation parents kept out of training. The initial baseline’s test split was evaluated once and recorded; future model choices must not be repeatedly tuned against that test result.

Simulator truths, random seeds, sample IDs, parent ancestry and parameter sidecars help validate experiments, but they are not model inputs. Giving a model the generating theta_E or a feature that nearly encodes it would not test inference from the image. The structured loader exposes model inputs and targets separately and keeps full provenance outside the model-input object.

The recorded test score answers a narrow question: “How well did this fixed image-only network recover theta_E for held-out images drawn from this synthetic proposal?” It does not answer “What is the mass of this observed galaxy?”, “How uncertain is the prediction?”, “Will this work on any Hubble image?” or “Does it generalize to the full lens population?”

### How the project parts fit together

The repository has two input paths and a shared analysis contract:

1. **Observed-data path:** FITS image → header/WCS inspection → curated lens-catalogue join → crop/pad, masks, background and variance products → release manifest → quality review.
2. **Synthetic-data path:** versioned model priors → lens/source rendering → PSF/background/noise → parameter and seed sidecars → release manifest → deterministic rerender/product validation.
3. **Shared contract:** both paths describe samples with schema-v2 manifests. The loader reads products and split membership while retaining whether each row is real or simulated and whether its target exists.
4. **Analysis path:** synthetic products feed controlled classical recovery and ML training; real products feed preprocessing/QC and the limited astrometric demonstration. The CNN trains only on the synthetic release.

This design lets reviewers compare products and processing rules without pretending that real and simulated images have the same calibration or scientific status. It ties each release to its configuration, manifest, split assignments, validation and product hashes.

### How to read the reported metrics

- A **manifest** is a table with one row per observation: identity, labels/status, product paths, metadata, eligibility and provenance.
- A **parent** is an independent simulated lens system. If noise/rotation/PSF variants are later made, they are descendants. An ancestry-aware split keeps a parent and related assets in just one split.
- **Train**, **validation** and **test** serve different roles. Train fits weights and normalization; validation compares models and selects checkpoints; test estimates performance only after model choice is frozen.
- **MAE** is average absolute error, here in arcseconds. **Bias** is signed mean error and can be near zero even if small radii are overpredicted and large ones underpredicted. **P95** is the 95th percentile absolute error and exposes tail failures.
- **Seed variation** measures how retraining changes the score on the same split. It is not automatically uncertainty over the lens population; three seeds are not an ensemble until a combined prediction method is declared and evaluated.
- A **passed release gate** means the specified structural, deterministic or split checks passed. It does not mean the simulation is astrophysically complete or real-data calibration is adequate.

### Glossary

| Term | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| CASTLES | Hubble Space Telescope lens observations/catalogue that supply local actual images and curated system information. |
| FITS / HDU | FITS is a common astronomy image/table format. An HDU is one image or data extension in a file; selecting the science HDU is part of ingestion. |
| WCS | World Coordinate System metadata mapping pixels to celestial coordinates. |
| PSF | Point-spread function: how telescope/instrument optics blur a point source across pixels. |
| SIS / SIE | Simplified spherical and elliptical lens mass-profile models used in scene generation and fitting. |
| Sersic profile | Mathematical surface-brightness profile used to represent extended galaxy light. |
| q and phi | Axis ratio and orientation of a model ellipse; they describe projected shape, not the CNN target. |
| External shear | A simple representation of tidal distortion from mass outside the main lens galaxy. |
| Arcsec | Arcsecond, an angular sky unit; 1 degree equals 3,600 arcseconds. |
| Einstein radius | Characteristic angular lens scale; for perfect alignment and a symmetric lens it is the ring radius. Here it is first treated as a model parameter. |
| Variance | Per-pixel estimate of noise spread. It describes pixel reliability; the real-release estimate is explicitly uncalibrated. |
| Ancestry leakage | Train/test contamination when related descendants or reused source/background assets land in different splits. |
| Domain shift | Differences between training simulations and telescope observations in optics, noise, calibration, morphology and sample selection. |
| SBI | Simulation-based inference: methods that learn distributions/posteriors from simulations rather than only one point prediction. It is future work here. |

### What a reader needs to reproduce the work

This summary lists paths and explains the workflow, but does not package multi-gigabyte images, arrays or every checkpoint. Reproduction requires the repository plus:

1. **Software:** Python 3.11 or newer as declared by the README; install core requirements and add simulation or PyTorch dependencies for those parts. The included run record is specifically Python 3.13.6 on Windows CPU.
2. **Actual observations:** supply the local CASTLES FITS tree at data/raw/castles/ to rebuild the real release. It is not guaranteed to be included in a Git clone.
3. **Simulation products:** regenerate releases with checked-in configs and lenstronomy 1.14.2, or supply the ignored generated product tree. The tracked engineering audit mirror contains manifests/reports/checksums, not every image array.
4. **ML checkpoint:** supply the matching best.pt for exact inference/evaluation. Checkpoints are ignored by Git, although this inspected workspace contains local checkpoint artifacts. Otherwise retrain from the config and matching dataset.
5. **Working directory:** run commands from the repository root because configs and manifests use relative paths.

A report, metrics CSV or preview is evidence about a run; alone it cannot rerun that experiment. Audit hashes help detect mismatches when the required files are supplied.

## 3. Purpose, target and scientific boundary

### 3.1 Intended target

The supervised target is **theta_E_arcsec**, the simulated lens model’s angular Einstein-radius parameter in arcseconds. For SIE simulations it is the parameter under the recorded mass model and convention. It is an angular lensing parameter, not an enclosed physical mass.

The schema keeps distinct:

- **theta_E_arcsec:** explicitly generated/model-defined truth for simulated rows, or a fully attributed fitted-model parameter if such a real result is later created.
- **einstein_radius_estimate_arcsec:** an observed, catalogue, literature or astrometric scale with an explicit estimation method.
- **mass_enclosed_msun:** a possible derived quantity requiring a declared aperture, lens/source redshifts and cosmology.

The present baseline has no physical-mass target. A catalogue estimate or CASTLES Size/2 value is not silently treated as simulator truth.

### 3.2 What the evidence supports

The checked-in evidence supports engineering statements such as:

- The real-castles-v2 release processed 137 observations from 69 lens systems and passed its structural product and fatal metadata gates while marking scientific/calibration issues for review.
- The sim-eng1000-v1 release contains 1,000 independent synthetic parents with 700/150/150 train/validation/test splits and no detected ancestry leakage.
- The classical recovery grid recorded 13 successful, locally identifiable optimizer fits in 13 cases. Its noiseless control had a maximum 0.033% relative Einstein-radius error; the worst noisy result reached 11.71%.
- An image-only CNN achieved a recorded 0.0876 arcsec MAE on the frozen synthetic test split. Its separate three-seed validation suite had mean MAE 0.09210 ± 0.00872 arcsec; the latter is sample standard deviation across seeds, not a confidence interval or ensemble score.
- Three preselected actual-observation peak-astrometry checks returned radii within the report’s 15% screening threshold of configured references.

These results do not demonstrate real-observation model accuracy, calibrated uncertainty, physical-mass accuracy, causal identification, arbitrary distribution-shift robustness, or population performance.

### 3.3 Explicit limits

- The local CASTLES products lack empirical PSF, ERR and DQ extensions. Thirty-seven metadata rows have unknown units; 17 lack telescope labels; validation also flags six ambiguous-redshift rows and four model-unsuitable systems.
- Actual data use a toy_unprofiled scalar variance fallback and an independent-pixel approximation. This is not a calibrated detector likelihood.
- Simulated sources and foreground light are analytic Sersic profiles; the PSF is analytic Gaussian; backgrounds are scalar; noise is independent Poisson plus read noise.
- Engineering priors are uniform hand-set ranges rather than a population and selection-function fit.
- The real comparison has three preselected systems and uses smoothed peak astrometry. HE0435 uses CASTLES Size/2 as a screening proxy; the method is not a pixel likelihood or posterior.
- Local Jacobian identifiability is not posterior coverage. The simulator does not capture all real morphology, detector, resampling, line-of-sight, selection or calibration effects.

## 4. Architecture and end-to-end workflow

### 4.1 Dependency direction

The architecture is intentionally layered:

1. src/data/schema.py defines the shared manifest contract.
2. src/processing/ and src/simulation/ create real and synthetic products that implement the contract.
3. src/modeling/ and src/ml/ consume contract-compatible releases.
4. src/pipeline.py coordinates public CLI operations; scientific calculations remain in their owning packages.

Conceptual flow:

    CASTLES FITS
      -> metadata extraction and curated lens catalogue
      -> enrichment and versioned preprocessing
      -> masks, background, variance, geometry and normalized arrays
      -> release manifest, lens-group splits and validation
      -> quality-control previews and bounded real astrometry check

    Versioned simulation priors
      -> SIS/SIE and source rendering
      -> foreground light, point images, PSF and detector noise
      -> reproducibility/truth sidecars and release manifest
      -> rerender validation and ancestry-safe splits
      -> classical parameter recovery
      -> truth-isolated ML dataset -> train/validate/evaluate

### 4.2 Public commands

Run from the repository root so repository-relative paths resolve correctly:

    python -m src.pipeline --help

The pipeline exposes eight command families:

| Command | Role |
|---|---|
| prepare-real | Build a versioned CASTLES metadata/catalogue/preprocessing release; validate products; make lens-level splits; optionally create review previews. |
| simulate | Generate one SIS, SIE, observation-effects or stress stage. |
| assemble | Combine simulation stage manifests into a release while retaining paths/provenance. |
| validate | Strictly open a release; simulated data also receive deterministic rerender validation. |
| make-splits | Create ordinary grouping or connected ancestry-component splits. |
| fit-grid | Run the fixed SIE recovery grid across P30/P60/P100 conditions. |
| real-comparison | Run the preconfigured exploratory peak-astrometry comparison. |
| engineering-release | Generate, validate, ancestry-split, checksum, freeze and mirror the 1,000-parent release. |

src/main.py is a compatibility wrapper that forwards to src.pipeline.main. ML also has module entry points: src.ml.train, src.ml.evaluate, src.ml.experiments and src.ml.compare.

### 4.3 Reproducibility and release safety

- Generated release directories are protected against accidental replacement unless --overwrite is passed.
- Release manifests use release-relative POSIX paths; moving products can invalidate manifest hashes/checksums.
- Run records include configuration hashes, counts, status and runtime.
- Simulations record independent parameter/noise seeds, truth and diagnostic sidecars, and ancestry identifiers.
- Rejections are logged and do not become accepted manifest rows.
- The engineering release records SHA-256 checksums and a tracked compact audit copy.
- Split creation can use the transitive closure of ancestry links such as split group, parent, source template and background template.
- Training provenance records environment, Git revision, source/config identity, release/split hashes and artifacts; evaluation/comparison checks identities and prediction hashes.
- Training statistics are computed from train only; validation selects checkpoints; the three-seed suite accesses zero test images.

## 5. Data contract and model interfaces

### 5.1 Manifest schema

Schema version **2.0** is a flat CSV interface. Its registry covers:

- Observation identity: sample, lens, domain, schema and release IDs.
- Raw/derived products: raw, science and processed paths; invalid, coverage and background masks; variance, expected variance, PSF, geometry, transform, background and noise sidecars.
- Array/instrument description: units, FITS HDU, dimensions, WCS, pixel scale in arcsec/pixel, coordinates, telescope/instrument/detector/filter, exposure, calibration and provenance.
- Lens/system science: source/lens type, environment, image count, confidence, model suitability, redshifts and their provenance.
- Targets: Einstein radius, axis ratio q, orientation phi_rad, ellipticity components, shear, optional aperture mass and explicit target-availability flags.
- Simulation provenance: model convention, simulator/version, parameter sidecar, parameter/noise seeds, parent IDs, template IDs and split ancestry.
- Quality/use: structural, observation and science status (pass, review, fail, unknown), allowed use roles and exclusion reason.

The stable image contract is a 256 × 256 float32 array. Arrays use NumPy [y, x] order; coordinate components are explicitly x/y, pixel coordinates are zero-based pixel centers, and angular quantities have declared units. The schema keeps missing values explicit and validates domain-specific requirements rather than fabricating labels.

The schema accepts domains real/simulated, status values pass/review/fail/unknown, and eligibility roles preprocessing/simulation/classical_fit/ml/real_comparison.

For completeness, the machine-readable registry fields are:

- Identity and ancestry: sample_id, lens_id, domain, schema_version, dataset_version, simulation_id, parent_system_id, parent_real_lens_id, source_template_id, background_template_id, split_group_id.
- Paths/products/instrument: raw_path, science_path, processed_path, mask_path, coverage_mask_path, background_mask_path, mask_semantics, variance_path, psf_path, psf_id, science_hdu, science_hdu_name, instrument, detector, filter_name, exposure_s, image_unit, calibration_status, calibration_source.
- Array geometry and WCS: original_shape, processed_shape, pixel_scale, pixel_scale_x, pixel_scale_y, pixel_scale_source, wcs_status, wcs_matrix_deg_per_pixel, center_x_px, center_y_px, center_ra_deg, center_dec_deg, geometry_transform_path.
- Processing/background/normalization/noise: processing_config_id, processing_version, background_status, normalization_path, masked_fraction, background_path, background_value, background_scale, background_valid_pixels, background_source_pixels, background_method, normalization_method, normalization_status, normalization_offset, normalization_scale, normalization_invertible, noise_model_path, variance_method, variance_status, variance_unit, noise_correlation_assumption.
- Lens/source science and targets: mass_model, theta_E_arcsec, einstein_radius_estimate_arcsec, einstein_radius_method, q, phi_rad, e1, e2, gamma1, gamma2, source_type, lens_environment, num_images, lens_confidence, model_suitability, ring_extended_flag, cropped_truncated_flag, classification_evidence, source_x_arcsec, source_y_arcsec, source_re_arcsec, source_n, lens_redshift, source_redshift, redshift_provenance, cosmology_id, mass_enclosed_msun, mass_aperture_arcsec, mass_target_available, theta_E_target_available.
- Simulation provenance and use status: simulator_name, simulator_version, parameter_seed, noise_seed, parameters_path, structural_status, observation_status, science_status, eligible_for, exclusion_reason.

### 5.2 Loader behavior

LensDataset selects release root, split, domain, eligibility and target fields; strict-product mode checks files and product metadata. It validates shapes/dtypes plus masks, variance, PSF and geometry when declared. Its safe get_sample() response separates:

- inputs.products: image/science arrays and optional mask, variance, PSF and geometry products.
- inputs.metadata: positive-allowlist metadata suitable for model input.
- targets: requested target values and availability flags.
- metadata: full row/provenance, potentially including privileged truth and identifiers.

Seeds, exact simulator nuisance parameters, ancestry, IDs and truth-sidecar paths are not model inputs. The historical __getitem__() interface returns an image and full row; get_sample() is the leakage-safe structured interface.

## 6. Physics, simulation and observations

### 6.1 Lens model conventions

src/simulation/models.py isolates the lenstronomy integration. The project records:

- SIS as the simple analytic control and SIE as the principal elliptical lens.
- Axis ratio q as minor/major.
- Ellipticity magnitude e = (1-q)/(1+q) and components e1 = e cos(2 phi), e2 = e sin(2 phi).
- Model coordinates in arcseconds, image arrays in [y, x], orientation in radians.
- Separate Cartesian external-shear components gamma1/gamma2.

The adapter validates scalar inputs, converts q/phi and e1/e2, checks backend conventions, and builds lens/light/point-source/PSF/image/fitting-sequence objects. Simulation requirements pin lenstronomy 1.14.2.

### 6.2 Staged simulator

configs/simulation_pilot_v1.yaml records the ladder:

- **P10 / SIS control:** analytic point-source and radius controls with unscaled output.
- **P30 / extended source:** SIE plus an extended Sersic source.
- **P60 / observation scene:** lens light, point images, Gaussian PSF, scalar background and count-space noise.
- **P100 / stress:** broader shear, source/lens morphology, brightness, PSF, noise and exposure ranges; separate from the matched training proposal.

The production-like sim-eng1000-v1 uses the validated P60-like range with one independent parent and one observation per parent. Its config sets 1,000 parents, seed 11001, split seed 4201, 70/15/15 fractions, unique analytic source/background/PSF per parent, target theta_E_arcsec and optional q/phi/ellipticity targets. P100 does not enter its splits.

### 6.3 Observation effects and saved products

Simulation outputs are organized by release into raw, science, normalized, masks, variance, expected variance, noise, PSF, geometry, transforms, background, scenes, parameters, diagnostics, previews and splits. Manifest rows reference these products. Truth/diagnostic JSON sidecars support rerender checks but must not leak to model inputs. The strict simulator validator checks schema, products, exact float32 rerender reproducibility (engineering tolerance 1e-10 arcsec), flux and image multiplicity.

### 6.4 Engineering release evidence

From data/manifests/sim-eng1000-v1/engineering_release.json:

- 1,000 requested, 1,000 accepted, 1,000 observations, zero rejections.
- Split counts: 700 train / 150 validation / 150 test; 1,000 effective ancestry groups; no cross-split leakage.
- All nine release gates passed, including unique sample/parent IDs and parameter/noise seeds, strict loading and simulation validation.
- Manifest SHA-256: 189c1351e768c6a6563c2af3243419df92d39f14a9670ff6385b693405e06a44.
- 21,009 checksummed artifacts, 2,573,791,870 bytes; recorded release/checksum runtime 773.6 seconds on the original local run.

- Frozen solver multiplicity: 5 singles, 778 doubles, 3 triples and 214 quads.

The full release under data/simulations/sim-eng1000-v1/ is local/ignored due to size. Its tracked compact audit mirror is data/manifests/sim-eng1000-v1/.

## 7. Real-observation preparation

### 7.1 Processing sequence

The actual-data pipeline inventories FITS files and selects a science HDU; extracts units, instrument/filter, exposure, WCS, pixel scale and provenance; validates/materializes the curated catalogue; joins labels without guessing; loads/hashes preprocessing config; applies common crop/pad geometry, masks, scalar background, variance and normalization; writes arrays/sidecars/manifest/run record; creates lens-level splits; validates fatal-vs-review metadata and products; and creates previews outside the release.

The configured real preprocessing is 256 × 256; uses automatic two-dimensional science-HDU choice; masks nonfinite data and padding; estimates a clipped scalar background; uses toy_scalar_background variance with an approximate independent-pixel assumption; applies masked 1st–99th percentile normalization; and records failures rather than adding partial manifest rows. Outputs live under data/releases/<release>/products/.

### 7.2 Current actual-data release

real-castles-v2 records:

- 137 observations / 69 lens systems.
- Lens-level splits: 94 train / 24 validation / 19 test for preprocessing/QC, not the current CNN training set.
- 91 rows pass and 46 are review-level; zero fatal metadata rows, zero strict product errors and zero preview errors.
- Review issue counts include 37 unknown units, six ambiguous-redshift rows and four model-unsuitable systems. Missingness includes 17 telescope labels. All 137 are eligible for preprocessing; 127 are recorded eligible for exploratory real comparison.
- Release manifest SHA-256: 1849ab21013ce282ec6fe98af7f24b767925e8045beec30c155d5c319c903d2e.
- Recorded creation runtime: about 52 seconds.
- Release notes prohibit interpreting toy variance as calibrated likelihood and require purpose-specific review for WFPC2 units and model suitability.

### 7.3 Real comparison

configs/real_comparison_v1.yaml freezes three selected F160W samples: B0218, HE0435 and Q2237. The implementation smooths/selects bright peaks, uses half-separation for doubles or a best-fit monopole circle for quads, and compares that angular scale with configured references. The report gives 0.148 arcsec vs 0.1581 for B0218 (6.3%), 1.201 vs 1.21 for HE0435 (0.8%), and 0.879 vs 0.85 for Q2237 (3.4%). All pass the configured 15% screen. This is a preselected exploratory sanity check, not a blind benchmark, physical-mass fit, calibrated likelihood or posterior.

## 8. Classical parameter recovery

src/modeling/fit_lens.py preserves an analytic SIS control and runs bounded least-squares SIE/SIE-plus-shear fits. It records optimizer convergence, runtime, objective/residual products, truth error, boundary status and local Jacobian rank/conditioning. The fixed grid covers P30 noiseless controls; P60 low/high SNR; P100 stress baseline; PSF-width mismatch; and source-profile mismatch.

Recorded grid result:

- 13 fits in six conditions; all 13 optimizer successes and locally identifiable; zero optimizer or non-identifiability failures.
- P30 noiseless max relative theta_E error: 0.00032996 (0.033%).
- Noisy-condition max relative error: 0.11710 (11.71%).
- Point image positions are conditioned on saved roots for observation fits; Jacobian diagnostics are local, not posterior coverage; source perturbations do not span real morphology.
- CSV, JSON, Markdown and residual NumPy arrays live under results/reports/fit-sie-grid-v1/. Earlier SIS/P30/P100 runs remain beside them.

## 9. Machine-learning implementation and results

### 9.1 Current model

The baseline is a 248,409-parameter four-block convolutional regressor:

- Input tensor shape [batch, 1, height, width], one processed image channel.
- Four downsampling blocks: 5×5 stride-2 convolution, GroupNorm, SiLU, then 3×3 convolution, GroupNorm and SiLU.
- Adaptive average pooling to 4×4 by default.
- Flattened head: 128-feature linear layer, SiLU, dropout 0.1 and scalar output.
- Default channels: 8, 16, 32 and 64.
- build_model() accepts kind cnn; unknown kinds fail explicitly.
- Training uses AdamW, batch size 16, learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0.0001, up to 20 epochs, patience 6. Baseline Huber delta is 1.0 on standardized targets; statistics are from training only.

It emits one point estimate, not an interval or posterior. src/ml/data.py currently supplies only the image to the baseline even though the shared loader supports declared auxiliary products.

### 9.2 Training/evaluation/experiment controls

- src/ml/train.py reads validated YAML, trains, selects by validation, and records predictions, curves, normalization, resolved config, summary and provenance.
- src/ml/evaluate.py verifies frozen checkpoint/data identities, evaluates a selected split and writes overall, subgroup and worst-case metrics.
- src/ml/experiments.py reads the registry; runs fixed validation-only seeds; verifies artifacts for resume; aggregates metrics/reports.
- src/ml/compare.py pairs candidates only when release/split/seed/sample/target identities match and prediction hashes verify.
- src/ml/losses.py implements Huber, MAE, MSE and log-cosh on standardized targets.
- src/ml/metrics.py implements MAE, median absolute/relative error, mean relative error, RMSE, bias, R², P90/P95, train-mean comparison, threshold fractions and target-bin metrics.
- src/ml/provenance.py records package/platform/device/Git/source identity; src/ml/plots.py creates diagnostics.

### 9.3 Recorded ML results

| Experiment | Evidence | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| theta-e-cnn-baseline-v1 | Selected epoch 19 of 20. Validation MAE 0.08836 arcsec; frozen test MAE 0.0876, RMSE 0.1292, median relative error 4.93%, bias −0.0090, R² 0.9127. | Same-proposal synthetic performance only. Test MAE is 77.2% below train-mean test baseline. Doubles are harder than quads; two low-radius doubles are positive-error outliers. |
| theta-e-cnn-seeds-v1 | Seeds 12001/12002/12003: validation MAE 0.08836 / 0.08587 / 0.10206; mean 0.09210, sample SD 0.00872. Mean P95 0.23782 arcsec. Test samples accessed: 0. | Seed variation on one fixed split, not a confidence interval or ensemble. Mean radius-bin bias: +0.0466 arcsec for [0.5,1.0), −0.0507 for [1.5,2.0]. |
| theta-e-huber-delta-050-v1 | Mean validation MAE 0.089680 vs reference 0.092097; paired gain 0.002417 arcsec. | Fails declared 0.01 arcsec MAE gate. Baseline remains selected. |
| theta-e-huber-delta-025-v1 | Mean validation MAE 0.085348; gain 0.006749. Mean P95 improves 0.01894 arcsec; worst-bin absolute bias essentially unchanged. | Also fails 0.01 MAE gate and increases out-of-prior fraction. Validation only. |
| theta-e-huber-delta-025-v1-smoke | Smoke-only reduced run. | Wiring/resume evidence, not a scientific result. |
| baseline-compatibility-v1 | Compatibility report, metrics, predictions and plot. | Historical compatibility evidence retained in results. |

The Huber-delta candidates changed one declared scalar setting while retaining baseline architecture, inputs, epochs, seeds and split. The comparison gate requires mean MAE gain at least 0.01 arcsec, no increase in mean P95 or mean worst-radius-bin absolute bias, and improved MAE for every seed. The project calls this a development rule, not a significance test.

### 9.4 ML result artifacts

Run directories retain resolved config/suite, normalization, epoch history, predictions CSV, training summary, curves, validation/evaluation plots, provenance and hashes, and checkpoints when present. Seed suites add one directory per seed, per-seed metrics, target-bin table, aggregate JSON, comparison figure and Markdown interpretation. best.pt is ignored by Git, so local presence does not imply a clean clone has it.

## 10. Infrastructure and runtime compatibility

### 10.1 Infrastructure footprint

This is a repository-local command-line research system. The inspected tree contains no Dockerfile, container orchestration, cloud templates, Terraform, database/server, queue, web/API service, package build metadata, lockfile or CI workflow. Runtime and data are local-filesystem based; CLI/config paths are repository-relative. Large raw/simulated data and some binary artifacts are not delivered by Git alone.

CPU suffices for documented runs; recorded environment is Windows AMD64 and PyTorch CPU. Device selection supports automatic choice and records the result. CUDA is an intended code path by dependency design, but no GPU benchmark evidence was found.

### 10.2 Python and dependencies

| File | Packages / purpose |
|---|---|
| requirements.txt | astropy ≥6.0, numpy ≥1.26, pandas ≥2.2, matplotlib ≥3.8, PyYAML ≥6.0, scipy ≥1.11; pytest ≥8.0; jupyter ≥1.0 and ipykernel ≥6.29. |
| requirements-ml.txt | PyTorch ≥2.8 and <3; CPU/CUDA wheel depends on package index and platform. |
| requirements-simulation.txt | Pinned lenstronomy==1.14.2. |

README says Python 3.11 or newer. Recorded ML provenance has Python 3.13.6, torch 2.8.0, NumPy 2.3.5, pandas 2.3.3, PyYAML 6.0.2 and matplotlib 3.10.8 on Windows CPU. Bytecode on disk is CPython 3.13.

Compatibility implications:

- Documented invocation is python -m src... from the repository root; there is no pyproject/setup installation contract or console script.
- Requirement files use lower bounds rather than a full lock. Except lenstronomy and torch’s major upper bound, versions may resolve differently; bitwise reproduction depends on the recorded environment and artifact hashes.
- Python ≥3.11 is declared support; experiment evidence verifies one Windows Python 3.13.6 environment, not every OS/Python/dependency combination.
- lenstronomy is pinned; configs specify locally default-disabled Numba JIT for reproducibility.
- Manifest paths use forward slashes even on Windows; code uses pathlib and assumes repository-root working directory.
- Jupyter is part of core requirements, but reproducible work belongs in src and the notebook is a planning artifact.

### 10.3 Repository hygiene

.gitignore excludes CASTLES/raw-like trees, normalized products, Python/pytest caches, generated simulations, release product directories, older derived products, preview PNG trees, model best.pt files, private notes, environment/secrets and the root q256 header. Configs, source labels, compact manifests, reports and evidence are generally retained. .gitattributes requests automatic text detection/LF normalization. pytest.ini points to tests and uses -ra.

Ignored does not mean scientifically irrelevant: local arrays, previews and checkpoints remain part of the observed workspace and are included in the file catalog.

## 14. Future plans in the project records

These items come from the experiment plan, implementation-plan notebook and model-landscape document. They are a research roadmap, not a claim that the work is implemented or scheduled.

### 14.1 Immediate controlled ML work

The documented next implementation is safe mask/variance input-channel adapters, then input ablations one factor at a time with model/loss/seeds/budget/splits fixed. Candidate inputs: invalid/coverage masks, variance, masks plus variance, training-only robust/asinh transformation, and a PSF kernel product. Do not use simulator-only scalar nuisances such as true PSF FWHM if those would be absent for real deployment.

The loss roadmap includes MAE/MSE/log-cosh comparison under the established protocol. The baseline Huber and two Huber-delta candidates exist, but neither delta candidate passed the conservative 0.01 arcsec mean-MAE gate.

The landscape recommends early controls/challengers:

1. Ridge/elastic-net and boosted trees on fixed auditable features.
2. Radial-profile MLP or 1D CNN.
3. Parameter-matched small residual CNN as the main learned challenger.
4. Rotation-equivariant residual model if it passes scalar and rotation-consistency gates.
5. Multi-scale CNN if paired gains justify it.

Begin with theta_E_arcsec alone, the existing train/validation split and established seeds. Report paired changes, every seed, tails, radius-bin bias, subgroups, runtime, parameter count and hashes. A lower headline MAE alone is not a sufficient winner.

### 14.2 Robustness, uncertainty and holdout

- Test PSF width/mismatch, noise, source brightness/morphology/position, lens light, image detectability and weak/missing counterimages, radius, physical vs detectable multiplicity, and separate P100 cases.
- Add uncertainty only after deterministic behavior is understood: deep ensemble, heteroscedastic output or quantile regression with coverage, interval width, calibration and error-uncertainty checks.
- Generate a new independent synthetic holdout; freeze candidate and protocol before opening it once.
- Compare the challenger with the train mean, baseline CNN, classical fits and P100 stress results.
- Write a model card with target/input definitions, data restrictions, subgroup/tail performance, calibration, compute and failure modes.

### 14.3 Real-data readiness

Bounded real exploration follows synthetic robustness. Real accuracy/mass claims need empirical PSF and detector/error products, calibrated variance/masks, greater observation realism, reviewed morphology/model suitability, realistic population/selection priors and a designed blind benchmark. Real angular predictions must remain exploratory until then.

### 14.4 Longer-term model families

The landscape proposes—but does not implement—a neural initializer followed by bounded physical refinement, then possibly a differentiable renderer hybrid. Before differentiable training: gradient-vs-finite-difference checks, noiseless known-source recovery, nuisance/source representation, matched controls and mismatch tests.

Uncertainty/posterior options include heteroscedastic regression, quantiles, mixture density, ensembles, BNN/MC dropout, Gaussian processes over compact features, and one-dimensional SBI (NPE/NLE/NRE) after simulation scale supports coverage/SBC checks. Multi-parameter outputs for q, orientation, shear and source variables should wait for scalar baselines and symmetry-aware targets. Physical mass also needs redshift/cosmology/aperture contract fields.

The docs defer large transformers, oversized generic ResNet, conventional PDE PINNs without a full forward observation model, high-dimensional flows trained on the current 700 parents, emulators presented as inverse predictors, and multi-parameter training before scalar baselines. These are scale/task-based deferrals, not permanent exclusions.

## 15. Practical reproduction map

The README and ML quickstart contain exact commands. Common paths:

- Create a venv; install requirements.txt; add simulation dependencies for simulator stages and ML dependencies for training.
- Run modules from the repository root using python -m.
- Build actual releases from data/raw/castles/ and source labels with prepare-real.
- Generate stages with simulate; validate manifests/products; use ancestry mode when parents/templates may be reused.
- Reproduce fit/comparison/engineering evidence using fit-grid, real-comparison and engineering-release.
- Train with configs/ml_baseline_v1.yaml; inspect validation diagnostics; use the existing frozen-test evaluation only as the recorded one-time result.
- Use the registry for fixed seed comparisons and a fresh output path for new runs; resume only when identity checks pass.

A clean checkout alone cannot run all data-dependent commands without the ignored CASTLES/simulation products being supplied or regenerated. Compact manifests and reports permit review without checking gigabytes of arrays into Git.

## 16. Interpretation cautions

- The inventory says what exists on disk; ignored files are not necessarily available from a clone.
- Metrics are transcribed from reports and were not recomputed for this summary.
- The existing test split has already been evaluated for the first CNN. Future selection uses train/validation and a new independent holdout.
- Three-seed standard deviation is seed sensitivity on one split; it is not a confidence interval, cross-split estimate or ensemble metric.
- Synthetic training is not real CASTLES/HST validation.
- A passed release means its declared engineering/structural gates passed; it does not remove scientific review/calibration limitations.
